summary:
MISSION ZERO: The Lunar Expedition is an educational 3D game developed in Unity 6 that transforms spacecraft engineering and lunar exploration into an interactive experience. Players take on the role of mission designers, configuring spacecraft systems, managing limited resources, and making engineering decisions that influence their mission. They explore essential spacecraft components, consider different routes to the Moon, face simulated mission risks, and experience the stages of a lunar expedition.

The project addresses the challenge of making complex space science and engineering concepts more accessible and engaging, especially for students and beginners. Instead of only reading about spacecraft, players learn by interacting with systems and seeing how their decisions affect the mission. MISSION ZERO encourages curiosity, critical thinking, problem-solving, and an understanding of how multiple engineering systems work together to make space exploration possible.
details:
Project Details – MISSION ZERO: THE LUNAR EXPEDITION

MISSION ZERO is an educational 3D space exploration game developed in Unity 6. It allows players to experience the decision-making involved in planning a lunar mission by taking the role of spacecraft designers and mission planners.

How It Works

Players begin by configuring a spacecraft through an interactive workshop. They can explore and manage eight major subsystems: propulsion, propellant tanks, solar panels, batteries, communications, navigation sensors, landing gear, and scientific payload. They must consider resource limits and engineering trade-offs when selecting components.

After configuring their spacecraft, players progress through a simulated lunar expedition. They encounter mission-planning decisions, compare different routes to the Moon, consider potential risks such as solar particle events, and experience key stages of the journey, including launch, spaceflight, lunar approach, and a landing scenario.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project makes space science and engineering more approachable through interactive learning. Rather than simply reading about spacecraft systems, players can explore components, make decisions, and understand how different systems depend on one another. It aims to encourage curiosity about space exploration while developing critical thinking, problem-solving, resource management, and systems-thinking skills.

Tools and Technologies

  • Unity 6: Main game engine and development environment.
  • C#: Programming language used for gameplay systems and interactions.
  • Universal Render Pipeline (URP): 3D rendering.
  • glTFast: Importing NASA-provided 3D models in GLB format.
  • NASA 3D resources: Earth and Moon models used to represent the planetary environments.

The project was developed as a desktop 3D game using software-based tools and assets; no specialized external hardware is required to play it.

Creativity and Design Considerations

MISSION ZERO combines spacecraft configuration, resource management, mission planning, and lunar exploration into one connected educational experience. Its visual direction draws inspiration from modern aerospace interfaces and spacecraft control systems, using a premium glass-inspired interface to make the experience feel immersive.

During development, the team considered accessibility for beginners, clarity of information, visual quality, resource constraints, the relationship between spacecraft subsystems, and the consequences of engineering decisions. The project uses simplified simulations to communicate engineering concepts in an engaging way rather than claiming to reproduce the accuracy of a real spacecraft or flight simulator.
